column1: 1. Couriers carry parcels between hubs. Run after the Rider and Logistics test sets, when parcels are At Hub at the origin hub and Logistics has created TRIP-1 (Test Data sheet). Hub staff steps are done with the Logistics 1 account.

2. Strict pass rule: a case passes only if EVERY point in its Expected Result is true. If any point is false, or something happens that the Expected Result does not mention (an extra record, a stock change, a wrong notification, an app crash or freeze, a server error), mark it Fail.

3. Check side effects, not just the screen: after each case, confirm the stock, order status, voucher usage, balances and the other roles' views named in the Expected Result. 'Nothing is saved' means the record is missing after a pull-to-pull-to-refresh, or after closing and reopening the screen.

4. Error messages must appear next to the field (or at the top of the form) and say what is wrong and how to fix it. A generic 'Something went wrong', a blank screen, an app crash, or a 500 error is a Fail even when the action was correctly blocked.
5. For 'Error Guessing' security cases, a correct block shows a 403 screen, a 'not found' screen or a redirect, and shows NO data from the other user's record anywhere on the screen.
6. Read the Assumptions sheet first. Rules A2 to A8 are the seven rules the module plan says must be agreed before testing; adjust any case whose rule differs from your system.
7. Seed the accounts, products, vouchers and shipping rates on the Test Data sheet before running the cases. Emails use example.com; read them from a mail catcher such as Mailtrap.
8. Test Case IDs follow <ROLE>-<MODULE>-<NNN>. Each module has positive, negative and boundary cases.
9. Fill in only the yellow cells: Actual Result, Status and Remarks. Pick the Status from the dropdown (Pass, Fail, Blocked, Not Run).

10. Pass = actual matches expected. Fail = it does not (describe what happened and add a screenshot or bug number in Remarks). Blocked = the case could not be run, for example because an earlier case failed.
11. The Results by module table above updates automatically from the Status column.

column2: Inputs are grouped into valid and invalid classes, and one value from each class is tested.
Values at and just beyond a limit are tested, for example ₱0.99, ₱1.00 and ₱1.01 for a ₱1.00 minimum price.
Combinations of conditions are tested, for example which vouchers can stack.
Changes in order or shipment status are tested, including transitions that must be blocked.
A complete user flow is tested from start to finish with valid data.
Likely mistakes are tested based on experience, for example double-tapping Place Order or changing an ID in a deep link or API request.

column1: 1. Install the build under test on at least one Android phone, and on an iPhone if your system supports iOS. Write the phone model, OS version and app build number in the Test run details above, and test on the same build throughout.
2. Copy every file on the Test Files sheet to the phone before testing: documents to the Files / Downloads folder and images to Photos (gallery).

3. Rows whose Test Scenario starts with [Mobile] are new mobile-only cases (keyboard, interruptions, no internet, permissions, camera, Back button, push notifications, deep links). Filter the Test Scenario column on '[Mobile]' to run them as a group. Assumptions M1 to M14 describe the rules they check.

4. 'Tap' is a single tap and 'double-tap' is two quick taps on the same button. 'Pull to refresh' means dragging the screen down from the top; if a screen has none, go back and reopen it. Use Airplane mode for the no-internet cases and turn it off before the next case.
5. Cases that send or capture an API request need a proxy tool on the phone (Assumption M11). If your group cannot capture app traffic, mark those cases Blocked and write 'no proxy' in Remarks.

6. Evidence: use the phone's screenshot or built-in screen recorder and name each file by case ID (for example buy-010.png or buy-031.mp4). Screen recordings are best for timing, interruption and no-internet cases.

column3: The accounts on the Test Data sheet already exist and are Active or Approved (they are the accounts created in the Account Creation test set). Seller 3 is Pending Approval and Rider 3 and Courier 3 are Suspended, for the negative cases. Reset the seeded products, stock and vouchers to their Test Data values before each module.
Per order: at most 1 store voucher per store, plus 1 platform voucher, plus 1 shipping voucher. Selecting a second voucher of the same type replaces the first; it never stacks.

Stock is deducted when the order is placed, for every payment method. It is restored when the order is cancelled (by buyer, seller or auto-cancel). For a Return-to-Sender or returned parcel, stock is restored when the seller confirms receipt. Stock can never go below 0.
Vouchers apply to items already on sale. Minimum spend is checked against the price actually paid (the sale or flash price), not the original price.

Sellers create flash sales for their own products in fixed time slots. When a product is in both a store sale and a flash sale, the flash price wins while flash quantity remains. Units beyond the remaining flash quantity in the same order are charged at the store sale price, or the regular price if there is no sale, and are shown on a separate line.

A buyer can cancel until the seller marks the order Ready for Pickup; after that there is no cancel option at all. A seller can cancel until the parcel is Picked Up. Unpaid e-wallet or card orders auto-cancel exactly 1 hour after the order is placed.
A product has at most 2 variation types, with 1 to 20 options per type. Store categories have at most 2 levels (category and subcategory). A product can belong to up to 3 store categories.

Store vouchers, sale discounts, flash sales and bundle discounts are seller-funded. Platform vouchers and shipping vouchers are platform-funded and never reduce the seller's earnings. A platform voucher on a multi-store checkout is split across the store orders in proportion to each store's merchandise subtotal, rounded to the centavo, with any rounding remainder given to the largest store. When only some items in an order are refunded, the store voucher is split across the items in proportion to their price, and the refund is the item price minus its voucher share.
Commission is 5% of the item subtotal after seller-funded discounts. Shipping fees are not part of the seller's gross sales. All money is rounded to 2 decimals (half up) per order.

Buyer tabs: To Pay → To Ship → To Receive → Completed (or Cancelled, Return/Refund). Seller: New → Accepted → Packed → Ready for Pickup. Shipment: Ready for Pickup → Assigned → Picked Up → At Hub → (In Transit → At Hub at the destination hub, when the address belongs to another hub; see A38) → Out for Delivery → Delivered (or Failed Delivery → Return to Sender → Returned to Sender). No status can be skipped or moved backwards except by a logged Logistics override.

The buyer taps Order Received, or the order completes automatically 7 days (168 hours) after Delivered. A return or refund can be requested only after Delivered, within those 7 days and before the order is Completed.

A review is allowed only for Completed orders, within 30 days of completion, one review per item. Stars (1–5) are required; text is optional, up to 500 characters; up to 5 photos. It can be edited once within the 30 days. The seller can post one reply per review and edit it; the seller cannot delete or hide a buyer's review.

Up to 3 delivery attempts. A reason from the list (Buyer not home, Wrong address, Refused) is required for every failed attempt. After the 3rd failed attempt, or immediately when the reason is Refused, the parcel is marked Return to Sender.

A job offer expires after 60 seconds. A declined or expired offer goes to the next nearest eligible rider; after 3 riders decline or let it expire, the job goes to the Unassigned queue for manual assignment. A rider holds at most 3 active jobs. Only Active, Online riders receive offers.

Earnings move from Pending to Available only when an order is Completed. Cancelled, returned and refunded amounts are excluded. A payout request must be at least ₱100.00 and no more than the Available balance, and only one payout request can be pending at a time.
Product, logo, banner, review, return, chat and proof-of-delivery images: JPG or PNG only (checked by file content, not just the extension), maximum 5 MB each. A product has 1 to 9 images.
Prices range from ₱1.00 to ₱1,000,000.00 with up to 2 decimal places. Stock and quantities are whole numbers from 0 to 99,999.

In vacation mode, products stay visible but Add to Cart and Buy Now are disabled with an 'On vacation' label, and checkout of items already in carts is blocked. A seller that is not Approved can save products only as drafts and cannot publish.

Deleting a store category that still has products moves those products to 'Uncategorized'. Deleting a parent category also deletes its subcategories. A product or a variant with unfinished orders cannot be deleted; other deletes are soft deletes, so order history still shows the product's name, image and price.

Shipping is charged per store, using the rate table on the Test Data sheet. Chargeable weight is the total actual weight of that store's items in the order, rounded up to the next whole kg. Rate changes apply only to checkouts started after the change.
A voucher used on a cancelled order is returned to the buyer's wallet if it has not yet expired, and its usage count is reduced by 1. A voucher is not returned for a refunded (returned) order.

Each role can open only its own screens; other roles get 403, an access-denied screen or a redirect, for both deep links and direct API requests. Users can open only their own records (orders, products, shipments, riders, couriers, trips). A session expires after 30 minutes of inactivity.
Every order or shipment status change sends an in-app notification and a push notification to each role involved, and to no one else. Emails use example.com and are read from the mail catcher.

Riders remit the full COD collected to their logistics company by the end of the day. Only the logistics company can confirm a remittance. Any difference between collected and remitted COD is flagged on the reconciliation screen.

Store name 3–30 characters (unique, not case-sensitive, spaces trimmed). Store description up to 500. Store category name 1–50 (unique per store, not case-sensitive, trimmed). Product name 5–120. Product description 20–3,000. Note to seller up to 200. Chat message 1–1,000. Free-text reasons (cancel, reject, override, suspend) 10–300. HTML or script entered in any field is shown as plain text.
4 to 12 letters and digits, no spaces or symbols, saved in uppercase. Codes are unique across the whole platform. Buyers can type the code in any case.

Once any buyer has claimed a voucher, the seller can only extend its end date or raise its usage limit; all other fields are locked. Ending a voucher removes it from the wallets of buyers who have not used it; orders already placed keep their discount.

A product can be in only one store sale at a time; overlapping schedules are rejected. A running sale's discount can be edited and applies immediately to new orders; End Now ends it at once. Orders already placed keep the price paid.
An alert is shown when a product's or variant's stock reaches 5 or fewer, once per crossing (it does not repeat until stock goes above 5 and drops again).

Up to 10 addresses per buyer. The default address cannot be deleted until another address is made default. Orders keep a copy of the address at order time, so editing or deleting an address does not change existing orders.

Reason from the list, a description of 10–500 characters, and 1 to 5 photos (JPG or PNG, 5 MB each) are required. The seller must respond within 3 days or the request is auto-approved. A rejected request can be escalated to a dispute once, within 3 days. The refund goes to the original payment method; for COD orders, to the buyer's refund account.

Delivered needs a photo (JPG or PNG) and the 6-digit delivery OTP shown in the buyer's app once the parcel is Out for Delivery. After 5 wrong OTP entries, OTP entry on that job is locked for 15 minutes.
₱50.00 per successful delivery, ₱30.00 per completed pickup, ₱0.00 for a failed attempt. Pay is not reduced by COD.

Auto-assign offers a job to the nearest Online, Active rider of the same company with fewer than 3 active jobs. Logistics can reassign a job only before it is Picked Up. Suspending a rider returns their not-yet-picked-up jobs to the Unassigned queue; parcels already picked up stay with that rider.

Every manual status override, rider or courier approval or suspension, trip reassignment or cancellation, seal or missing-parcel discrepancy, rate change and remittance confirmation is logged with user, date and time, old value, new value and reason. Log entries cannot be edited or deleted from the UI.
Reports export as CSV and XLSX. Exported rows and totals equal the on-screen rows and totals for the same filter.

Every create or submit action (Publish, Place Order, Pay, Request Payout, Accept job, Remit, Confirm) is idempotent: double-tapping, tapping the keyboard's Done key twice, pulling to pull-to-refresh, or going Back and resubmitting never creates a second record or a second charge.

A parcel whose delivery address belongs to another hub travels between hubs on a linehaul trip driven by a courier. Logistics creates the trip (origin hub, destination hub, and parcels that are At Hub at the origin and belong to the destination hub's delivery zone), then assigns a courier. The courier accepts, scans every parcel while loading, enters the seal number and departs; each parcel becomes In Transit. At the destination, hub staff confirm the seal and scan each parcel in (At Hub). Trip statuses: Scheduled → Assigned → Accepted → Loading → In Transit → Arrived → Completed (or Completed with Discrepancy, or Cancelled). A trip can be edited or cancelled only before departure.

Only Active couriers who are On Duty can be assigned a trip; a courier holds at most 1 active trip, and the trip weight cannot exceed the vehicle's load capacity. Going On Duty needs location permission and a passed pre-trip checklist (Tires, Lights, Brakes, Fuel, Cargo door lock); an item marked Not OK needs a note (10–300 characters), keeps the courier Off Duty and notifies Logistics. Off Duty is not allowed while a trip is Loading or In Transit. Depart is allowed only within 500 m of the origin hub and after every parcel is scanned; Arrived only within 500 m of the destination hub. Suspending a courier returns their Assigned or Accepted trips to Unassigned; a trip already In Transit stays with them until handover. Only hub staff can confirm receipt at the destination. Plate and license numbers are unique across riders and couriers.

The seal number is BH- followed by 7 digits (for example BH-0004521) and is required before departure. If the seal entered at the destination does not match, the trip is flagged Seal Discrepancy. Parcels not scanned in when the destination hub closes receiving become Missing in Transit; a parcel marked Damaged needs a photo. Any discrepancy makes the trip Completed with Discrepancy, notifies Logistics and the seller, and asks the courier for a note (10–300 characters). All are logged (A35).

Pay per completed trip: Van ₱600.00, 4-Wheeler Closed Van Truck ₱1,000.00, 6-Wheeler Truck ₱1,500.00. Declined, cancelled and reassigned-away trips pay ₱0.00; the pay goes to the courier who completes the handover. A delay report needs a reason from the list (Heavy traffic, Vehicle breakdown, Weather, Road closure, Other) and a new ETA later than the current time; Logistics is notified. After a Vehicle breakdown report, Logistics can reassign the In Transit trip to another courier, who must scan every parcel again before continuing.

The system is tested as a mobile app (Android and/or iOS) installed from an APK, TestFlight or store build. Record the phone model, OS version and app build on the Summary sheet. Admin-only steps (approvals, platform vouchers) may stay on a web admin panel; run those steps there.

Each field opens the keyboard that fits it: email keyboard (with @) for Email; number pad for Mobile Number, OTP, Postal Code, TIN, quantity and stock; decimal pad for prices and weight. Password fields show no autocorrect or suggestions. The keyboard never hides the focused field or the main button.

The OTP field accepts a pasted 6-digit code (filling every box when the field is split into boxes) and supports the phone's one-time-code autofill where available. The expiry countdown is based on the time the code was sent, so it keeps running while the user is in the mail app.

Sending the app to the background (Home, switching apps, an incoming call, locking the screen) and returning keeps the current screen and the typed values (passwords may be cleared). Rotating the phone is either blocked (portrait only) or keeps every value. Nothing is submitted unless the user taps the button.

column2: No internet or a dropped connection
column3: With no connection the app shows a clear no-internet message with Retry, never crashes or freezes, and never shows success for something the server did not save. Saving an action offline and sending it later is allowed only if the app shows it as pending, and it is sent exactly once. Write in column D whether your app blocks or queues offline actions.

Camera, photos/files, location and notifications are requested only when first needed, with a reason. If a permission is denied, the app explains why it is needed, offers a link to the phone's Settings, keeps working for everything that does not need it, and never crashes.

Each upload offers Camera, Gallery/Photos and, for PDFs, Files. The type and size rules (A10 / A16) apply to every source. Camera photos larger than 5 MB are compressed to 5 MB or less before upload. Copy the Test Files to the phone before testing.

The Android Back button and iOS swipe-back go to the previous screen. Leaving a form with unsaved changes asks the user to confirm discarding them. After logging out, Back never shows a logged-in screen.

The app stays logged in after it is closed, reopened or the phone restarts, until the user logs out, the password is changed (which also ends the session on the user's other phones), or the session token expires.

Status changes, approvals and chat messages also send a push notification to the phone of each user involved, and to no one else. Tapping a notification opens the related screen, even if the app was closed. If notifications are turned off in phone Settings, the in-app notification list still works.

Share links and email links (activation, product, store) open the matching screen in the app, or a mobile web page if the app is not installed. Access rules are enforced by the server: a deep link or a direct API request for another role's or another user's data is refused (401/403, an access-denied screen or a redirect to home). Cases that capture or send a request directly need a proxy tool on the test phone (for example HTTP Toolkit, Charles or mitmproxy). If your group cannot capture app traffic, mark those cases Blocked and write 'no proxy' in Remarks.

Every screen works on a small phone (about 5.5 in) and a large one (about 6.7 in), in light and dark mode, and with the largest system font: no cut-off text, no overlapping controls, and no buttons hidden behind the keyboard.

The rider app needs location permission to go Online and sends the rider's location while Online. If location is turned off, or the app is closed for more than 5 minutes, the rider receives no new offers and is shown as Offline. Navigate opens the phone's map app (Google Maps or Waze).

Waybill barcodes are scanned with the phone camera (with a flashlight toggle), and every scan screen also lets the user type the tracking number. Proof-of-delivery and damage photos are taken live with the in-app camera; old photos from the gallery are not accepted.
